complexity.notes: Appending with `self.items[key] += [(timestamp, value)]` builds a throwaway one-element list each call; a `defaultdict(list)` plus plain `append((timestamp, value))` is tidier. The hand-rolled binary search could be replaced by `bisect_right` from the stdlib, which would shorten get considerably. Worst-case figure reflects adversarial collisions on input-controlled string keys degrading dict lookups.
complexity.summary: Each key maps to a list of (timestamp, value) pairs kept sorted because set timestamps arrive in strictly increasing order; get binary-searches that list for the largest stored timestamp not exceeding the query. This is the asymptotically optimal approach for the problem.
complexity.time_average: O(1) per set, O(log n) per get
